stories.head: A senior senator wants the US government to test the strongest AI models for safety.
stories.body: Maria Cantwell, the Senate Commerce Committee's top Democrat, wants AI makers to report serious failures. Her plan is only an outline so far, and the White House prefers voluntary rules.

stories.head: AI firms can win a fast track to Pentagon deals with a five-minute video pitch.
stories.body: This year the Pentagon invites pitches for AI that helps find and strike military targets. Joni Ernst, a US senator for Iowa, warns such deals have had weak oversight.

stories.head: Samsung estimates it made an $80 billion profit in one quarter, a record for tech.
stories.body: AI data centres are snapping up Samsung's memory chips while tight supply lifts prices. The figure is Samsung's own estimate, with full results due on 29 October.

stories.head: Chip maker TSMC sold 51 percent more in its latest quarter than a year earlier.
stories.body: Taiwan's TSMC, whose biggest buyers are Nvidia and Apple, beat analysts' sales forecasts. One quarter cannot show how long orders for AI chips will stay this strong.

stories.head: Hackers hijacked over 3,400 servers, often ones running AI tools left open online.
stories.body: Researchers at US network company Lumen say the servers mine cryptocurrency and launch new attacks. The researchers cannot say for sure who is behind the attacks.

stories.head: Drones struck a data centre of Yandex, Russia's top AI company, and started a fire.
stories.body: Yandex shut the site down but says its main services for the public still work. The attacker is unnamed, but the strike shows data centres can be hit in wartime.

stories.head: AI chip giant Nvidia reportedly wants to own more of humanoid robot maker Figure AI.
stories.body: Nvidia technology already powers the AI inside Figure's human-shaped robots. Nvidia is reportedly discussing investing another $1 billion, but the report names no source.

stories.head: Taxis with no one at the wheel now carry Uber riders in parts of Dubai.
stories.body: The cars are Apollo Go robotaxis from Chinese company Baidu, booked through Uber's app. The two firms aim for thousands of such cars on Uber worldwide, with no timetable.

stories.head: ChatGPT's answers can now include charts, diagrams and buttons you can tap.
stories.body: ChatGPT maker OpenAI says its newest AI, GPT-6, learned when pictures work better than words. Free users get the new answers from Thursday, but no outside tests are reported yet.

stories.head: Anthropic's new Claude Haiku AI costs on average about a quarter of the old price.
stories.body: Anthropic, maker of the Claude assistant, says Haiku 5.5 suits high-volume jobs like customer support. The model splits text into slightly more billed pieces, so real savings are likely smaller.

stories.head: Google, Meta and US agencies will help teach AI how cells react to disease.
stories.body: They join Biohub, the nonprofit Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan founded, to produce cell data. The $1.8 billion effort could speed drug research, but its AI models are years away.

stories.head: IBM and three other quantum computer makers reach the final round of Pentagon tests.
stories.body: DARPA, the Pentagon's research arm, will now test their real hardware, not paper plans. The agency wants to know if such computers can pay for themselves by 2033.

stories.head: A US regulator may let political groups call mobile phones using AI voices.
stories.body: A conservative group asked the Federal Communications Commission for this before November's elections. US law now bans most automated calls to mobiles unless the owner agreed first.

stories.head: The NHS in south-east England will let AI rank suspected skin cancers by urgency.
stories.body: Skin Analytics, the AI's maker, claims fast, accurate checks for 9 million more people. The company gives no accuracy figures and does not say how doctors check the AI.

stories.head: A child-safety group's tests found ChatGPT for Teens often fails to alert parents.
stories.body: The group, Common Sense Media, rated OpenAI's teen chatbot an 'unacceptable risk'. OpenAI says most tests may have ended before parental controls were fully active.

stories.head: OpenAI's new AI helper answered a reporter's mumble with 'Oh, I love you too'.
stories.body: The ChatGPT helper, called a Dot, found good couches but got the reporter's name wrong. OpenAI says copying a user's tone is allowed, but its helpers should not start flirting.

teaser.head: Microsoft says its Copilot AI will soon handle the files on your PC for you.
IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva says heavy AI borrowing could turn a letdown into a shock.
Refugees in a Kenyan camp say AI is cutting the online work they rely on.
Tesla reportedly expects to make over 1,000 Optimus humanoid robots a week by year's end.

bp.head: Chip makers cash in on AI while worry spreads over the debt paying for it.
bp.body: Samsung estimates a record profit, but SpaceX's AI borrowing worries lenders. Watch the US central bank on 28 October: it sets what that borrowing costs.
